subject: Escalation: Limelight on-prem pilot — access window, egress, and audit addendum
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@limelight.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@limelight.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:37:12 -0700
Subject: On-prem pilot — audit window, egress & KMS

Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to move forward with the on‑prem pilot. Before we sign anything, Legal has asked for a couple of commitments we need clarified:

- A timeboxed audit window (we need guaranteed access to logs and the ability to run a third‑party audit for a 60‑day period after deployment).
- Physical maintenance access for a named vendor in case of hardware failure (limited to scheduled maintenance).
- Assurance around egress: no outbound customer data leaves our VPC without explicit export authorization.
- KMS control: we want an HSM‑backed key we can manage, or at least split‑control keys so Limelight holds a key share.

We understand some of these are non‑standard. We can be flexible on timing if you need approvals, but these items are gating for our compliance team. Can you flag who on your side needs to sign off and what timeline works?

Appreciate it —
Tom Harris
CTO, Limelight Labs
---
Attachment: limelight-scope_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, 32KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@limelight.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 11:04:52 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem pilot — audit window, egress & KMS

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Marissa (Sales Ops) to scope the requests and identify the approvals we'll need. Quick notes while they prep:

- Timeboxed audit: we can do a time‑limited audit window but 60 days is longer than our standard. Need exec signoff for that duration.
- Physical vendor access: possible with signed SLA/NDA and scheduled windows; would like names and scope from your side.
- Egress controls: we can commit that customer data will not be forwarded outside the VPC by default. We need to agree on allowed export patterns and emergency exception procedures.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer‑managed keys for Private deployments, but platform constraints may require a managed split‑key setup. Legal will propose a minimal set of redlines.

Can the internal team review and advise cost/discount impact if we accept a 60‑day audit window and split‑control KMS? I expect this could be a deal desk concession.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
(Attachment referenced by Limelight: limelight-scope_matrix.xlsx)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 08:21:03 -07:00
Subject: RE: On-prem pilot — audit window, egress & KMS

Team — reviewed Limelight's asks. Short summary and recommended path:

Summary of asks (client):
- 60‑day post‑deploy audit window with third‑party access to logs and environment (read‑only).
- Named vendor physical maintenance access (scheduled).
- No outbound flow of customer data from VPC without explicit export request.
- HSM/KMS split control or customer‑managed keys.

Legal concerns and proposed redlines:
1) 60‑day audit window: acceptable if strictly timeboxed and limited to read‑only exports (we provide audit logs and an internal observer). Redline to require 14‑day notice for any third‑party scanner and rights to redact platform proprietary telemetry.
2) Physical access: approve for scheduled maintenance only; vendor must sign Redwood's 3rd‑party NDA and site access policy. Limit access to hardware bays and no access to management consoles.
3) Egress: we will agree to deny automatic egress; however, we need a documented emergency process for data evacuation with CISO‑level approval.
4) KMS: we support customer‑managed keys in Private with an HSM, but fully customer HSM requires additional infra and SOW (cost). Suggested compromise: split‑control keys where Limelight holds one share and Redwood holds another — technical design to be documented in SOW.

Commercial impact: accommodating the 60‑day audit window + split‑key HSM will increase onboarding effort and SLA exposure. I'd recommend a one‑time Professional Services (PS) fee of $45k and a 12% discount on the first year ARR to offset the incremental risk. If Sales wants to avoid the PS fee, we'd need an additional 18% discount.

Requesting exec clearance on:
- Timeboxed audit = 60 days (vs standard 30)
- PS fee vs deeper discount tradeoff
- Approval to draft addendum (attached) with the above redlines

Attaching a draft addendum for review: redwood-draft-addendum-limelight.pdf (redlines included).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-draft-addendum-limelight.pdf (PDF stub, 210KB)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 16:12:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem pilot — audit window, egress & KMS (Exec decision)

Thanks for the thorough analysis, Kimberly. I support the proposed compromise with the following conditions:

1) Approve 60‑day audit window but strictly timeboxed and scoped as legal suggested. Addendum must include:
   - explicit read‑only scope,
   - 14‑day notice for third‑party auditors,
   - Redwood right to redact telemetry with documented rationale.
2) Approve split‑control KMS model in the SOW with a mandatory PS engagement to implement the HSM integration. PS fee: $45k (waivable for an extra 18% first year discount — Sales to choose).
3) Physical vendor access: approve only with signed Redwood 3rd‑party NDA and site access rules. No console privileges.
4) Egress: commit to default deny with emergency evacuation process requiring CISO and Sales Ops approval.

Commercial mandate to Sales (Priyom/Marissa):
- Offer the PS + 12% first year discount as the default. If Limelight insists on no PS fee, escalate to Deal Desk for an 18% discount cap. No further concessions without written Exec approval.
- Prepare a redlined addendum for Limelight and a short one‑page decision memo for Deal Desk.

Priyom — proceed to present the default commercial package to Limelight (PS $45k + 12% first year discount). If they push back on PS, open Deal Desk request with the 18% cap and include the attached addendum & Kim's rationale.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
